reading.body:
QTS Suwanee Data Center 1 is part of a 53-acre campus in Gwinnett County with 50+ MW of critical capacity today and 100+ MW planned. If the planned expansion reaches completion, this single campus would represent roughly 150% of Georgia's currently published data center capacity of 66.3 MW across four facilities, making it a material concentrator of AI infrastructure in the state. The facility sits in Georgia's Atlanta metro region, where QTS has held operations since its early 2000s acquisition phase.

The campus publishes 50+ MW of existing capacity, which ranks fifth by announced megawatts among Georgia facilities. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 50 MW of IT load translates to approximately 1,250 racks. The planned doubling to 100+ MW would bring that to 2,500 racks, a scale sufficient to host a substantial model training cluster or distributed inference workload. No certification or tenant information is published for this facility.

Georgia has 33 mapped data center facilities but only four with published capacity figures, making this campus one of very few whose power footprint is documented. The operator, Quality Technology Services, is controlled by Blackstone as of 2021 and operates across multiple states. Whether this campus matters to AI depends on whether the planned expansion proceeds and which tenants it serves, neither of which is published.
